name: opencode-plugin-api-v2
body:
The apg opencode tool suite runs as an opencode 2.x plugin. Each suite tool file under `opencode-suite/tools/` default-exports a plugin definition — `Plugin.define({ id, setup(ctx) })` imported from `@opencode/plugin` — whose `setup` registers its one tool through `ctx.tool.transform(editor => editor.add({ name, description, input, execute }))`. The registered tool carries a name, a description, a JSON-Schema `input` object, and an `execute` that returns structured content (`{ content }`). Each tool keeps its own file, its own stable plugin id, and its own import of the shared lib, so the suite holds one plugin per tool file (the plugin granularity decision).

The shared lib `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` sources the project location from the opencode 2.x plugin context — `ctx.location.directory` and `ctx.location.project` in place of the V1 `{ directory, worktree }` tool context — and a tool's own optional `directory` argument stays the authoritative project directory (the base the curated tools rebase stored repo-relative identities onto, `requirements.requirement.absolute-paths-at-tool-boundary`). The plugins close over their `setup(ctx)` context for the location.

The filesystem tools (`apg_rm`, `apg_mv`, `apg_cp`) read the acting agent's effective permission scope through the opencode 2.x agent/permission surface, so their self-enforced scope (`requirements.requirement.agent-fs-write-operations`, `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`) holds on opencode 2.x, and the pure `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` decision stays the same.

Acceptance criteria: every `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` file imports `Plugin` from `@opencode/plugin` and default-exports `Plugin.define({ id, setup })`; `setup` registers its tool through `ctx.tool.transform` with a JSON-Schema `input` and an `execute` returning `{ content }`; `opencode-suite/lib/apg.ts` sources the project location from the opencode 2.x plugin context; `opencode-suite/package.json` depends on `@opencode/plugin`; the fs tools' scope read uses the opencode 2.x permission surface and the pure `fsScopeDecision` semantics are unchanged.
